rows.en: The ocean is heating up.
rows.zh: 海洋正在升温。

rows.en: That's the conclusion of a new study that finds that Earth's oceans now 26 heat at twice the rate they did 18 years ago. Around half of ocean heat intake since 1865 has taken place since 1997, researchers report online in Nature Climate Change.
rows.zh: 这是一项新研究得出的结论：地球上的海洋如今吸收热量的速度是 18 年前的两倍。研究人员在《自然·气候变化》网站上报告说，自 1865 年以来海洋吸收的热量中，约有一半发生在 1997 年之后。

rows.en: Warming waters are known to 27 to coral bleaching (珊瑚白化) and they take up more space than cooler waters, raising sea 28 While the top of the ocean is well studied, its depths are more difficult to 29 The researchers gathered 150 years of ocean temperature data in order to get abetter 30 of heat absorption from surface to seabed.
rows.zh: 众所周知，变暖的海水会导致珊瑚白化，而且暖水比冷水占据更大的空间，推高海平面。虽然海洋表层已被充分研究，但它的深处更难探索。

rows.en: They gathered together temperature readings collected by everything from a 19th century 31 of British naval ships to modem automated ocean probes.
rows.zh: 研究人员收集了 150 年的海洋温度数据，以便更好地把握从海面到海底的热量吸收全貌。

rows.en: The extensive data sources, 32 with computer simulations ( 计算机模拟), created a timeline of ocean temperature changes, including cooling from volcanic outbreaks and warming from fossil fuel 33
rows.zh: 他们汇集了各种来源的温度读数——从 19 世纪英国海军舰船的一次航行，到现代的自动化海洋探测器。这些海量的数据来源与计算机模拟相结合，绘制出一条海洋温度变化的时间线，其中包括火山爆发带来的降温与化石燃料排放造成的升温。

rows.en: About 35 percent of the heat taken in by the oceans during the industrial era now resides at a 34 of more than 700 meters, the researchers found.
rows.zh: 研究人员发现，工业时代海洋吸收的热量中，约 35% 目前储存在 700 米以深的地方。

rows.en: They say they're 35 whether the deep-sea warming canceled out warming at the sea's surface.
rows.zh: 他们表示，尚不能确定深海升温是否抵消了海面的升温。

rows.en: A) South Korean city designed for the future takes on a life of its own A) [A] Getting around a city is one thing—and then there’s the matter of getting from one city to another.
rows.zh: 在一座城市内出行是一回事，而城市与城市之间的通行则是另一回事。关于未来理想城市的一种设想，是提供一个便于搭乘飞机出行的地点。

rows.en: One vision of the perfect city of the future is a place that offers easy access to air travel. In 2011, a University of North Carolina business professor named John Kasarda published a book called Aerotropolis: The Way We’ll Live Next.
rows.zh: 2011 年，北卡罗来纳大学一位名叫约翰·卡萨达的商学院教授出版了一本名为《航空城：我们未来的生活方式》的书。

rows.en: Kasarda says future cities should be built intentionally around or near airports.
rows.zh: 卡萨达说，未来的城市应有意围绕机场或在机场附近建设。

rows.en: The idea, as he has put it, is to offer businesses “rapid, long-distance connectivity on a massive scale.”
rows.zh: 正如他所表述的，其理念是为企业提供“大规模、快速、远距离的连接”。

rows.en: B) “The 18th century really was a waterborne（水运的）century, the 19th century a rail century, the 20th century a highway, car, truck century—and the 21st century will increasingly be an aviation century, as the globe becomes increasingly connected by air,” Kasarda says.
rows.zh: “18 世纪的确是水运的世纪，19 世纪是铁路的世纪，20 世纪是公路、汽车与卡车的世纪——而随着全球通过航空联系日益紧密，21 世纪将越来越成为航空的世纪，”卡萨达说。

rows.en: Songdo, a city built from scratch in South Korea, is one of Kasarda’s prime examples.
rows.zh: 松岛是韩国一座从零开始建设的城市，是卡萨达的主要范例之一。

rows.en: It has existed for just a few years.
rows.zh: 它仅存在了几年时间。

rows.en: “From the outset, it was designed on the basis of connectivity and competitiveness,” says Kasarda. “The government built the bridge directly from the airport to the Songdo International Business District.
rows.zh: “从一开始，它就是基于连通性与竞争力设计的，”卡萨达说，“政府修建了从机场直抵松岛国际商务区的桥梁，地面基础设施与新机场同步建成。” 松岛距韩国主要国际枢纽仁川机场仅一步之遥。

rows.en: And the surface infrastructure was built at the same time as the new airport.
rows.zh: 但要成为未来之城，仅靠邻近机场还远远不够。

rows.en: C) Songdo is a stone’s throw from South Korea’s Incheon Airport, its main international hub (枢纽）. But it takes a lot more than a nearby airport to be a city of the future.
rows.zh: 仅仅把一个地方建成“国际商务区”并不意味着它就会成为那样的区域。朴渊秀早在 1986 年就构想出了这座未来之城。

rows.en: Just building a place as an “international business district” doesn’t mean it will become one. Park Yeon Soo conceived (构想）this city of the future back in 1986. He considers Songdo his baby.
rows.zh: 他把松岛视为自己的孩子。

rows.en: Park sees himself as a visionary.
rows.zh: 朴自视为一个有远见的人。

rows.en: Thirty years after he imagined the city, Park’s baby is close to 70 percent built, with 36,000 people living in the business district and 90,000 residents in greater Songdo.
rows.zh: 在他构想这座城市三十年后，他的“孩子”已建成近 70%，商务区居住着 3.6 万人，大松岛区有 9 万居民。

rows.en: It’s about an hour outside Seoul, built on former tidal flats along the Yellow Sea.
rows.zh: 它位于首尔约一小时车程外，建在黄海沿岸昔日的滩涂上。

rows.en: There’s a Coast Guard building and a tall trade tower, as well as a park, golf course and university.
rows.zh: 那里有海岸警卫队大楼和一座高耸的贸易塔，还有公园、高尔夫球场和一所大学。

rows.en: D) Chances are you’ve actually seen this place.
rows.zh: 你很可能其实见过这个地方。

rows.en: Songdo appears in the most famous music video ever to come out of South Korea.
rows.zh: 松岛出现在韩国有史以来最著名的音乐视频中。

rows.en: “Gangnam Style” refers to the fashionable Gangnam district in Seoul.
rows.zh: 《江南 Style》指的是首尔时尚的江南区。

rows.en: But some of the video was filmed in Songdo.
rows.zh: 但视频的某些场景是在松岛拍摄的。

rows.en: “I don’t know if you remember, there was a scene in a subway station.
rows.zh: “我不知道你是否记得，地铁站里有一幕。

rows.en: That was not Gangnam. That was actually Songdo,” says Jung Won Son, a professor of urban development at London’s Bartlett School of Planning.
rows.zh: 那不是江南，那其实是松岛，”伦敦大学学院巴特莱特规划学院的城市发展教授郑元善说，“在那里拍摄的部分原因是它崭新又漂亮。” 这座城市本应成为全球公司的枢纽，员工来自世界各地。

rows.en: “Part of the reason to shoot there is that it’s new and nice.”
rows.zh: 但结果并非如此。松岛的名声是一座未来主义的鬼城。

rows.en: E) The city was supposed to be a hub for global companies, with employees from all over the world.
rows.zh: 但现实要复杂得多。一座带有巨大浅蓝色环形结构的桥梁通向商务区。

rows.en: But that’s not how it has turned out.
rows.zh: 主干道中央，是一长排世界各国的旗帜。

rows.en: Songdo’s reputation is as a futuristic ghost town. But the reality is more complicated.
rows.zh: 街角有一家星巴克和一家 7-11——都是如今在世界各地随处可见的国际品牌。

rows.en: A bridge with big, light-blue loops leads into the business district. In the center of the main road, there’s a long line of flags of the world.
rows.zh: 这座城市并不空旷。有推着婴儿车的母亲、拄着助行器的老妇——即便在白天气温高达 90 华氏度时也是如此。

rows.en: On the comer, there’s a Starbucks and a 7-Eleven—all of the international brands that you see all over the world nowadays.
rows.zh: 卞英镇担任松岛房地产协会主席，并在该城市 2005 年第一期开放时就开始在此卖房。

rows.en: F) The city is not empty.
rows.zh: 他说过去几年需求激增。

rows.en: There are mothers pushing baby carriages, old women with walkers—even in the middle of the day, when it’s 90 degrees out. Byun Young-Jin chairs the Songdo real estate association and started selling property here when the first phase of the city opened in 2005. He says demand has boomed in the past couple of years.
rows.zh: 他的大多数客户是韩国人。

rows.en: Most of his clients are Korean. In fact, the developer says, 99 percent of the homes here are sold to Koreans.
rows.zh: 事实上，开发商表示，这里 99% 的房屋卖给了韩国人。年轻家庭搬来是因为学校很好。

rows.en: Young families move here because the schools are great. And that’s the problem: Songdo has become a popular Korean city more popular as a residential area than a business one.
rows.zh: 而这正是问题所在：松岛已成为一座受欢迎的韩国城市，作为住宅区比作为商务区更受欢迎。

rows.en: It’s not yet the futuristic international business hub that planners imagined.
rows.zh: 它还不是规划者所设想的未来国际商务枢纽。

rows.en: “It’s a great place to live.
rows.zh: “这是个宜居之地。

rows.en: And it’s becoming a great place to work,” says Scott Summers, vice president of Gale International, the developer of the city.
rows.zh: 而且它正成为一个宜业之地，”该城市开发商盖尔国际的副总裁斯科特·萨默斯说。

rows.en: The floor-to-ceiling windows of his company’s offices overlook Songdo Central Park, with a canal full of small boats and people fishing.
rows.zh: 他公司办公室的落地窗俯瞰松岛中央公园，运河里满是小船和垂钓的人。

rows.en: Shimmering (闪烁的）glass towers line the canal’s edge.
rows.zh: 闪烁的玻璃塔沿着运河边缘排列。

rows.en: G) “What’s happened is that our focus on creating that quality of life first has enabled the residents to live here,” Summers says.
rows.zh: “所发生的是，我们先专注于创造那种生活质量，才让居民能够在此居住，”萨默斯说。

rows.en: But there needs to be strong economic incentives for companies to locate here.
rows.zh: 但这里仍需要有强有力的经济激励，企业才会落户。

rows.en: The city is still unfinished, and it feels a bit like a theme park.
rows.zh: 这座城市尚未完工，感觉有点像主题公园。

rows.en: It doesn’t feel all that futuristic.
rows.zh: 它并不那么具有未来感。

rows.en: There’s a high-tech underground trash disposal system.
rows.zh: 这里有一套高科技地下垃圾处理系统。

rows.en: Buildings are environmentally friendly.
rows.zh: 建筑是环保的。

rows.en: Everybody’s television set is connected to a system that streams personalized language or exercise classes. H) [H] But this is not Star Trek.
rows.zh: 每个人的电视机都连接到一个系统，可播放个性化的语言或健身课程。但这并非《星际迷航》。

rows.en: And to some of the residents, Songdo feels hollow.
rows.zh: 对一些居民来说，松岛让人感到空洞。

rows.en: “I’m, like, in prison for weekdays.
rows.zh: “我嘛，工作日就像坐牢。

rows.en: That’s what we call it in the workplace,” says a woman in her 20s.
rows.zh: 我们在职场就是这么叫它的，”一位二十多岁的女性说。

rows.en: She doesn’t want to use her name for fear of being fired from her job.
rows.zh: 她不愿透露姓名，生怕被解雇。她每个周末都回首尔。

rows.en: She goes back to Seoul every weekend. “I say I’m prison-breaking on Friday nights.”
rows.zh: “我说我周五晚上是在‘越狱’。”但她得开着自己的车去“越狱”。

rows.en: But she has to make the prison break in her own car.
rows.zh: 连接松岛与仅 20 多英里外的首尔之间没有高铁。

rows.en: There’s no high-speed train connecting Songdo to Seoul, just over 20 miles away. I) [I] Park Y eon Soo, the man who first imagined Songdo, feels frustrated, too.
rows.zh: 最早构想松岛的朴渊秀也感到沮丧。

rows.en: He says he built South Korea a luxury vehicle, “like Mercedes or BMW.
rows.zh: 他说他为韩国打造了一辆豪华座驾，“就像奔驰或宝马。

rows.en: It’s a good car now.
rows.zh: 现在它是辆好车。

rows.en: But we’re waiting for a good driver to accelerate.” But there are lots of other good cars out there, too.
rows.zh: 但我们在等一位好司机来加速。”但市面上也有许多其他好车。

rows.en: The world is dotted with futuristic, high-tech cities trying to attract the biggest international companies.
rows.zh: 世界上遍布着试图吸引最大国际公司的高科技未来城市。

rows.en: J) Songdo’s backers contend that it’s still early, and business space is filling up—about 70 percent of finished offices are now occupied.
rows.zh: 松岛的支持者辩称现在还为时尚早，商务空间正在填满——已完工办公室约 70% 现已入驻。

rows.en: Brent Ryan, who teaches urban design at MIT, says Songdo proves a universal principle. “There have been a lot of utopian (乌托邦的）cities in history.
rows.zh: 在麻省理工学院教授城市设计的布伦特·瑞安说，松岛印证了一个普遍原则。

rows.en: And the reason we don’t know about a lot of them is that they have vanished entirely.” In other words, when it comes to cities—or anything else—it is hard to predict the future.
rows.zh: “历史上有过许多乌托邦式的城市。我们对其中许多一无所知，原因是它们已彻底消失。”换言之，无论对于城市还是其他任何事物，未来都难以预测。

rows.en: The U. S. and China don't agree on much these days.
rows.zh: 美国和中国如今在许多问题上意见不一。

rows.en: Germany and France share a border and a currency but are frequently at odds.
rows.zh: 德国和法国共享边界和货币，却常常争执不下。英国和印度喜欢各行其是。

rows.en: The U. K. and India like to march to their own drum.
rows.zh: 但有一个问题，所有这些国家都看法一致：科技公司规模太大、权力太大、利润太高。而且这种权力只会愈发增强，使各国政府别无选择，只能正面应对：把相关公司告上法庭、通过新的竞争法，甚至可能拆分科技巨头。

rows.en: But there9s one issue on which all these countries see eye to eye: Technology companies are too big, too powerful, and too profitable.
rows.zh: 中国是最新一个实施反垄断打击的国家，上月公布了反垄断规则。

rows.en: And that power is only likely to intensify, leaving governments with no choice but to confront it head-on by taking the companies to court, passing new competition laws, and perhaps even breaking up the tech giants.
rows.zh: 在这些规则草案出台之前，亿万富翁马云旗下的蚂蚁集团一笔370亿美元的股票发行被意外叫停，这清楚表明，没有任何公司能够逃避政府的监管。

rows.en: China is the latest to implement an anti-trust crackdown, unveiling anti-monopoly rules last month.
rows.zh: 中国此举正值美国和欧洲加大力度约束亚马逊、苹果、脸书和谷歌之际。

rows.en: The draft rules followed the surprise suspension of a $ 37 billion stock offering by billionaire Jack Ma's Ant Group Co., making clear that no company can evade the government's regulation.
rows.zh: “巨头们变得越来越大，却没有变得更好，”德国欧洲议会议员安德烈亚斯·施瓦布说。他曾推动2014年一项拆分谷歌的决议。

rows.en: The moves in China coincide with accelerating efforts in the U. S. and Europe to rein in Amazon, com, Apple, Facebook, and Google. “The big get bigger and bigger but without being better,says Andreas Schwab, a German member of the European Parliament who championed a 2014 resolution to break up Google, “Growing economic power, growing influence on local markets all over the world, and a growing concern of competitors and consumers altogether have made it happen now.^^ In this new anti-trust era, the old focus on pricing power no longer applies, because several of the biggest tech companies have established trillion-dollar monopolies by charging consumers next to nothing.
rows.zh: “经济实力不断增长，对世界各地本地市场的影响力不断增强，竞争对手和消费者也日益担忧，这些因素共同促成了现在的局面。” 在这个新的反垄断时代，过去对定价权的关注已不再适用，因为几家最大的科技公司已经通过几乎不向消费者收费而建立起万亿美元级别的垄断。科技巨头正越来越多地在银行、金融、广告、零售和其他市场占据强势地位，迫使较小企业依赖它们的平台来接触客户。

rows.en: Tech giants are increasingly assuming powerful positions in banking, finance, advertising, retail, and other markets that force smaller businesses to rely on their platforms to reach customers. For years, Europe alone confronted the power of digital giants.
rows.zh: 多年来，只有欧洲独自面对数字巨头的力量。各国政府感到震惊的是，欧洲公司既无法匹敌硅谷的创新，也无法阻止谷歌和脸书攫取个人数据，并借此获得广告收入。

rows.en: Governments were alarmed that European companies were failing to match Silicon Valley's innovations or to stop Google and Facebook from vacuuming up personal data and, with that, advertising revenue.
rows.zh: 在欧盟竞争事务负责人玛格丽特·维斯塔格带领下，各国试图监管市场并鼓励公平竞争。

rows.en: Led by Margrethe Vestager, the European Union's competition chief, countries have sought to police the market and encourage fair play.
rows.zh: 在中国，这场打击至少部分源于对本土科技行业变得过于强大的担忧。

rows.en: In China the crackdown has been driven at least partly by fear that the homegrown tech industry is becoming too powerful.
rows.zh: 中国长期以来支持阿里巴巴和腾讯，但它们大量积累中国公民数据，令北京日益担忧。

rows.en: The country has long championed Alibaba and Tencent, but their massive accumulation of data on the Chinese citizenry is a growing concern for Beijing.
rows.zh: 在美国，新一代反垄断专家认为，应当考虑隐私、数据控制、劳动者权利以及对较小企业的整体影响。

rows.en: In the U.S., a new breed of anti-trust experts argues that consideration should be given to privacy, control over data, workers'rights and the overall impact on smaller companies And the public in general have grown increasingly skeptical of social media companies More than 60% say the sector has a negative effect on the country, and almost half want more regulation for social media, according to a 2020 Pew Research Center study
rows.zh: 而且公众对社交媒体公司越来越持怀疑态度。皮尤研究中心2020年的一项研究显示，超过60%的人认为该行业对国家有负面影响，近一半人希望对社交媒体加强监管。

rows.en: The term“environmentalist” can mean different things.It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems.In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy.
rows.zh: “环保主义者”一词可以有不同的含义。它过去指那些努力保护野生生物和自然生态系统的人。

rows.en: The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers'basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing.
rows.zh: 进入21世纪，该词的含义已演变，涵盖了应对人为气候变化的必要性。这两种环保主义之间的区别，是科学界在核能问题上产生分歧的原因。

rows.en: Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
rows.zh: 一方是纯粹主义者，他们认为核能风险太大，不值得，解决气候危机的唯一方案是可再生能源。另一方同意可再生能源至关重要，但表示，当没有阳光、没有风时，社会需要一定量的电力来满足消费者的基本需求。

rows.en: “Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables,” he said.“If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear.”
rows.zh: 核能远比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁，是一个自然的选择，尤其是在水电能力有限的地区。曾协助撰写联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会报告的莱昂·克拉克并非核能的不加批判的支持者，但他表示，如果我们真的想实现碳中和，核能是一个有价值的选择。

rows.en: The achievability of universal 100%renewability is similarly contentious.
rows.zh: “所有这一切的核心是，你认为我们实际上能在多大程度上实现100%可再生能源的气候目标，”他说。“如果你认为我们做不到，而你又关心气候，你就不得不考虑核能之类的方案。”普遍实现100%可再生能源的可行性同样存在争议。

rows.en: Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been“100%renewable” for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal.
rows.zh: 像佛蒙特州伯灵顿这样的城市多年来一直“100%使用可再生能源”。但这些城市往往人口稀少，偶尔仍依赖化石燃料能源，并且拥有丰富且可就地利用的可再生资源。

rows.en: Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
rows.zh: 与此同时，能够依靠可再生能源运行的国家通常得益于非凡的水电能力。

rows.en: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables.
rows.zh: 德国是大型工业化国家推动绿色能源的最佳案例研究。总理安格拉·默克尔于2011年宣布了“能源转型”计划，该计划将逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时逐步引入可再生能源。

rows.en: Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400%since 2010, and renewables provided 46%of the country's electricity in 2019. But progress has halted in recent years.
rows.zh: 自2010年以来，风能和太阳能发电量增长了400%以上，2019年可再生能源提供了该国46%的电力。但近年来进展停滞。

rows.en: The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity.
rows.zh: 可再生能源的不稳定性不仅意味着夜间往往无法发电，还意味着太阳能和风能在白天可能使电网不堪重负，迫使公用事业公司付费让客户用电。

rows.en: Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
rows.zh: 滞后的电网基础设施难以将过剩的绿色能源从德国北部输送到工业发达的南部，这意味着许多工厂仍在使用煤炭和天然气。一些地方也达到了政治上的极限，民众以大声抗议来反对新建风力涡轮机。

rows.en: The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5%since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
rows.zh: 结果是，自2010年以来，德国的温室气体排放量下降了约11.5%——低于欧盟13.5%的平均水平。

rows.en: Effective Friday, Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) has declared a strike against 11 video game publishers over games that went into production after Feb. 17, 2015. The companies include some of the heavyweights of the industry, like Electronic Arts Productions, Insomniac Games, Activision and Disney.
rows.zh: 自周五起，美国演员工会及广播电视艺人联合工会（SAG-AFTRA）宣布对11家电子游戏发行商发起罢工，涉及2015年2月17日之后投入制作的游戏。这些公司包括业内一些重量级企业，如艺电制作公司、失眠症游戏公司、动视和迪士尼。

rows.en: The strike comes in light of an unsuccessful 19 months of negotiations after the existing labor contract known as the Interactive Media Agreement expired in late 2014. overall, the strike is an effort to provide more secondary compensation along with other concerns, such as transparency upon hiring talent and on-set (制作中) safety precautions. The video gaming industry has ballooned in recent years.
rows.zh: 此次罢工源于既有的劳动合同《互动媒体协议》于2014年底到期后，长达19个月的谈判未能取得成功。总体而言，这次罢工旨在争取更多的追加酬金，并涉及其他诉求，例如在聘用演员时保持透明以及制作中的安全保障措施。

rows.en: The Los Angeles Times reports that the industry is in the midst of an intense increase in cash flow. In 2015, gaming produced $23.5 billion in domestic revenue.
rows.zh: 近年来，电子游戏产业急剧膨胀。《洛杉矶时报》报道称，该行业正处于现金流激增之中。

rows.en: But SAG-AFTRA says voice actors don’t receive residuals (追加酬金) for their gaming work.
rows.zh: 2015年，游戏产业在美国国内创造了235亿美元的收入。

rows.en: Instead, they receive a fixed rate, which is typically about $825 for a standard four-hour vocal session.
rows.zh: 但SAG-AFTRA表示，配音演员没有因游戏作品获得追加酬金。

rows.en: So the voice actors are pushing for the idea of secondary compensation—a performance bonus every time a game sells 2 million copies or downloads, or reaches 2 million subscribers, with a cap at 8 million. “It’s a very small number of games that would trigger this secondary compensation issue,” said voice actor Crispin Freeman, who’s a member of the union’s negotiating committee.
rows.zh: 相反，他们拿的是固定报酬，通常一场标准的四小时配音工作约为825美元。

rows.en: “This is an important aspect of what it means to be a freelance (从事自由职业的) performer, who isn’t regularly employed every single day working on projects.” Another major complaint from the actors is the secrecy of the industry.
rows.zh: 因此，配音演员们正在推动追加酬金的想法——每当一款游戏的销量或下载量达到200万份，或订阅用户达到200万时，就发放一笔绩效奖金，上限为800万。

rows.en: “I can’t imagine if there’s any other acting job in the world where you don’t know what show you’re in, when you’re hired,” says voice actor Keythe Farley, who chairs the SAG-AFTRA negotiating committee. “And yet that happens every day in the video game world,” Farley told reporters during a press conference Friday.
rows.zh: “能够触发这种追加酬金的游戏数量非常少。”配音演员、工会谈判委员会成员克里斯平·弗里曼说，“这是作为一名自由职业表演者的重要方面，自由职业者并不是每天都有固定的项目工作。”演员们的另一大不满是这个行业的保密性。

rows.en: “I was a main character in Fallout 4, a character by the name of Kellogg, and I never knew that I was doing vocal recording for that game throughout the year and a half.”
rows.zh: “我无法想象世界上还有哪种表演工作，在你被雇用的时候却不知道自己在演什么节目。”担任SAG-AFTRA谈判委员会主席的配音演员基思·法利说。

rows.en: Scott Witlin, the lawyer representing the video game companies, says voice actors “represent less than one tenth of 1 percent of the work that goes into making a video game.” So “even though they’re the top craftsmen in their field,” Witlin says, “if we pay them under a vastly different system than the people who do the 99.9 percent of the work, that’s going to create far more problems for the video game companies.”
rows.zh: “然而在电子游戏行业，这种情况每天都在发生。”法利在周五的新闻发布会上对记者说，“我曾是《辐射4》中的一个主要角色，名叫凯洛格，但在那一年半的时间里，我从来不知道自己在为这款游戏做配音录制。”代表游戏公司的律师斯科特·维特林表示，配音演员“在制作一款电子游戏的全部工作中所占的比例不到千分之一。”因此，“尽管他们是业内顶尖的工匠，”维特林说，“如果我们用一套与承担99.9%工作的人截然不同的薪酬体系来支付他们，那将给游戏公司带来更多问题。”
